label: lem:cauchy_integral_to_pole_sum
title: Cauchy integral approximation by finite pole sums
statement:
Let \(K \subset U \subset \C\), with \(K\) compact and \(U\) open. Let
    \(f : \C \to \C\) be holomorphic on \(U\). Then for every \(\eps > 0\), there
    exist finitely many points \(a_1,\dots,a_N \in \C \setminus K\) and coefficients
    \(c_1,\dots,c_N \in \C\) such that
    \[
      \forall z \in K,\qquad
      \left|
        \sum_{j=1}^N \frac{c_j}{z-a_j} - f(z)
      \right| < \eps .
    \]
proof:
\leanok
    By \cref{lem:cauchy_grid_representation}, fix a finite oriented contour
    \(\Gamma = \bigcup_i [A_i, B_i] \subset U \setminus K\) such that
    \[
      f(z)
      = \frac{1}{2\pi i}\sum_i \int_{A_i \to B_i}
        \frac{f(\zeta)}{\zeta-z}\,d\zeta
    \]
    for every \(z \in K\). Given \(\eps > 0\), apply
    \cref{lem:segment_pole_sum_uniform_approx} to each segment \([A_i, B_i]\)
    with target error \(\eps/(m+1)\), where \(m\) is the number of segments,
    obtaining finitely many poles on the segment and coefficients whose pole
    sum approximates the per-segment contour integral. Concatenating across
    segments and applying the triangle inequality yields the desired total
    approximation.
notes: Signature: `lemma cauchy_integral_approximated_by_pole_sum {K U : Set ℂ} {f : ℂ → ℂ} (hK : IsCompact K) (hU : IsOpen U) (hKU : K ⊆ U) (hf : DifferentiableOn ℂ f U) : ∀ ε > 0, ∃ (N : ℕ) (a : Fin N → ℂ) (c : Fin N → ℂ), (∀ j, a j ∉ K) ∧ ∀ z ∈ K, ‖(∑ j, c j / (z - a j)) - f z‖ < ε`. Finite collection of poles/coefficients encoded as `Fin N → ℂ`. Holomorphy via `DifferentiableOn ℂ f U`.
